look_here_first: Start with shorter OBLONG or linear-oblong leaves and a rhizomatous bushy or low perennial habit. Magnify UPPER stem, peduncle and phyllary for STALKED GLANDS, and check outer often leaf-like phyllaries. Against S. patens, the strongest discriminator is leaf attachment: patens has clearly HEART-SHAPED deeply clasping upper leaves; oblongifolium may clasp SLIGHTLY. Do not treat glands alone as unique to this species—patens can also be glandular.

best_field_traits: Perennial, often low and densely branched, spreading by rhizomes.
Short oblong to linear-oblong leaves, often rough and aromatic when handled; compare lower and upper leaves.
Stalked glandular hairs on upper stems, peduncles and phyllary faces are high-value ID features.
Heads with ray and disc florets; involucres roughly (5-)7-9 mm in FNA treatment; verify with scale and glands.

comparisons.key_distinctions: S. patens var. patens can be densely stipitate-glandular, and var. gracile sparsely glandular; do not teach 'patens usually nonglandular' as absolute. Compare patens's strongly cordate/auriculate clasping upper leaf bases with oblongifolium's relatively oblong shorter leaves and usually mild clasping, then use rootstock, outer leafy phyllaries, and measured involucre.
